title: LIRIL Documentary — guided tour of the record
voice_intro: This is LIRIL. You are entering a documentary of the public record — watchable as a film, navigable as a site. Every claim is meant to land on a primary source.

chapters.title: Cold open — the contract
chapters.narration: Welcome to TENET5. This is not a blog. It is an operational intelligence record of Canadian public power — procurement, health policy, foreign influence, and accountability — built so a daily viewer can know what the federal government is doing and where the multi-year path points. LIRIL will walk you through the structure, the active files, and the future map.

chapters.title: What is happening right now
chapters.narration: Start here every day. The daily briefing sheet answers three questions: what Ottawa announced or contracted; which investigation cluster it attaches to; and what decision comes next. Defence spending ladders, Arctic build-out, and the Griffon helicopter pause are the current gravity wells.

chapters.title: Live OSINT seal
chapters.narration: The OSINT dashboard is the live seal: threat level, thread counts, findings vault. When feeds are stale, the seal says so honestly. Agentics and PRISM self-train against this public tail — the website is both report and training surface.

chapters.title: Primary file — Griffon GLLE
chapters.narration: Primary investigation: CH-146 Griffon Limited Life Extension. Official numbers freeze at up to ninety million for definition and eight hundred million for implementation, full operational capability planned for twenty twenty-seven, fleet of eighty-five. In June twenty twenty-six the government paused the upgrade citing cost, schedule, complexity, and replacement fleet planning. That pause is now the primary point in a four-point procurement velocity cluster.

chapters.title: Procurement as pattern
chapters.narration: Zoom out. Defence procurement is not one helicopter. Arctic over-the-horizon radar, submarine competition framing, airborne early warning signals, and life-extension pauses form a cluster: money and speed rise together, public competition paper trails thin. Watch announcements against signed contracts.

chapters.title: Future plans map
chapters.narration: Stated plans: climb the NATO spend ladder toward two percent, then four percent class by around twenty thirty, with five percent defence and security related language by twenty thirty-five. Arctic infrastructure, long-range strike, sovereign satellite communications, and a defence industrial strategy convert politics into factories and basing. Inferred risks — labeled inference, not court findings — include spending ratios outrunning readiness, sole-source velocity, and industrial capture. A daily reader should leave knowing the next decision points: pause lift or replacement definition, contract awards, Budget tables, committee heat.

chapters.title: The wider record — Article II frame
chapters.narration: The site's long-form thesis maps systemic harm onto the five elements of the Genocide Convention Article Two — killing, harm, conditions of life, preventing births, transferring children — using government and court sources. You do not need to accept every legal framing to use the primary documents. The standard is: every claim traces to a primary page.

chapters.title: Evidence vault
chapters.narration: The evidence index is the vault. Hundreds of pages, source-cited. When LIRIL narrates, it is reading structure that was built to survive scrutiny — not vibes.

chapters.title: Agentic systems — public tail of PRISM
chapters.narration: This website is also a demonstration: agentic systems maintain a real public surface; local C++ and p256 pipelines train against the work. Theme contract QUANTANIUM — pristine ice lake — is locked so machines cannot drift the brand into neon garbage.

chapters.title: Close — how to watch daily
chapters.narration: Ritual for a daily viewer: open the daily briefing; read happening-now; scan the metrics rail; open the future plans horizon; check whether any cluster point moved from open to primary. Then watch or navigate the documentary again when a major file updates. You should leave knowing exactly what Ottawa is doing this week — and what the multi-year map claims next.
